clue.text: Retired, finally, after serious cut

indicators.note: after places the picked letter at the end, following the synonym

parts.note: a serious problem is a severe one

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word Retired

explanation.surface: Someone retired and was then hit by a serious pay or budget cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Severed means cut off or sliced through, the past participle of sever, a synonym of cut.

clue.text: Learned person's sort of power involving church

indicators.note: involving means enveloping, so the power word wraps round church

parts.note: solar power is a kind of power from sunlight

explanation.surface: An academic's favoured energy source somehow involves the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar is an erudite person, someone deeply versed in an academic subject.

clue.text: Warm beverage? Lot prepared squash

indicators.note: prepared hints at the letters being made up afresh like a dish

explanation.surface: A hot drink? A whole batch made from squash, the cordial.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on squash as a British fruit cordial drink; the definition is the gourd.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegetable marrow is a large gourd, a type of squash grown in British gardens.

clue.text: Change back row

parts.note: the rear is the back
a range is a row, as of mountains or houses

explanation.surface: An instruction to alter the back row of seats or players.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearrange is to alter the order or layout of things, a form of change.

clue.text: Put off, cleaner gent ignored

indicators.note: ignored means left out, so the word gent drops from the cleaner

parts.note: detergent is a cleaner

explanation.surface: A man put off by cleaning products is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter someone is to discourage them, putting them off doing something.

clue.text: Collection of books in one large vehicle

definitions.meaning: an ... edition gathers several books in a single volume
the full old name for a bus

explanation.surface: A bookmobile: a load of books carried around in one big vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Omnibus names both a single volume reprinting several works and the passenger road vehicle shortened to bus.

clue.text: Carrying too much? Load never varied

indicators.note: varied means changed in form, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Is this overburdened? The load never changed.
explanation.definitionFit: Overladen means loaded beyond capacity, burdened with an excessive weight or cargo.

clue.text: Cold Pepsi? Every other one over in New York

indicators.note: in places the turned letters within the abbreviation
over in a down clue means turned upside down, so the picked letters run backwards
every other one takes alternate letters of Pepsi, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A chilled Pepsi? Every second one is finished over in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Every other one' picks PPI; 'over' turns it to IPP, set 'in' NY.
explanation.definitionFit: Nippy is British informal for chilly, describing weather sharp and cold enough to nip.

clue.text: A licensed bowling alley may provide such fun

definitions.text: A licensed bowling alley may provide such fun

parts.words: A licensed bowling alley may provide such fun
parts.note: a licensed venue serves alcohol and a bowling alley has pins, so it literally offers both, and the phrase also means carefree enjoyment

explanation.surface: A pub with a bowling alley promises a jolly night out.
explanation.walkthrough: Licensed means allowed to sell alcohol; skittles is a British pub game like ninepin bowling. The idiom, as in life is not all fun, means easy pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names easy pleasure and enjoyment, literally the drink and pins game a pub alley offers.

clue.text: Postpone having to invest across America

indicators.note: across means stretching over, so the spending word straddles America

parts.note: to invest money is to spend it
US is short for United States, America

explanation.surface: A financier delays putting money into American ventures.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspend something is to defer it or halt it temporarily, which is to postpone it.

clue.text: Speak after fighting in rickety ghost train

indicators.note: after puts the synonym for speak at the end of the answer
rickety means shaky and unsound, so these letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: fighting is war
taken as written
to express something is to speak it

explanation.surface: Someone speaks up after a scuffle on a creaky fairground ghost train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ghost train' looks like the definition, a fairground ride; only 'train' defines, and 'ghost' is fodder for 'rickety'. 'after' puts the speaking word last.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hogwarts Express is the steam train carrying pupils to school in the Harry Potter books.

clue.text: Roof worker losing face, by and by

indicators.note: losing face says the first letter, the front of the word, is dropped

parts.note: a slater lays slates on roofs

explanation.surface: A roofer is humiliated, and things will work out by and by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing face' drops the S at the front of SLATER.
explanation.definitionFit: By and by is an old idiom for eventually or at a future time, which is what later means.

clue.text: Rarely beaten, champion in team event

indicators.note: beaten suggests the letters are whipped up and reshaped

parts.note: an ace is a champion or expert

explanation.surface: A champion who is seldom defeated is competing in a team contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A relay race is run by a team of athletes, each covering one leg in turn.

clue.text: Outlaw, Scott's Roy, popular gangster

parts.note: Sir Walter Scott wrote the novel Rob Roy, so his Roy is Rob
popular things are in
hood is slang for a gangster or hoodlum

explanation.surface: A list of famous rogues: an outlaw, Scott's Rob Roy, and a well-liked mobster.
explanation.walkthrough: Rob Roy is a Walter Scott novel about a Scottish outlaw, so the name before Roy is ROB.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Hood is the legendary English outlaw of Sherwood Forest who robbed the rich.

clue.text: Prudent to give support to unmarried mother differently?

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting word sits beneath, so it comes last
M is the abbreviation for married, so unmarried takes it away

parts.note: taken as the word itself before its letter is dropped
prudent means wise

explanation.surface: Is it sensible to support a single mother some other way?
explanation.walkthrough: 'unmarried' drops M (married) from MOTHER, giving OTHER; 'to give support to' puts WISE below it.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherwise means in another way, which is what differently also means.

clue.text: Wound up in section of weekend edition

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something was concluded in one part of the Saturday newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind up a meeting or business is to bring it to a close, so wound up means finished.

clue.text: Senior manager's do, around four

indicators.note: around says the doing word goes round the numeral

parts.note: to execute a task is to do it
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A boss's party, starting around four o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'do' as a party, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An executive is a senior person in a company with authority to take decisions.

clue.text: Make a fuss evacuating a Greek island

indicators.note: evacuating means emptying out, so the letter a is cleared from the word

parts.note: to create is British informal for making a fuss

explanation.surface: Tourists kick up a fuss while being evacuated from a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech 'to create' means to make a scene or complain loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: Crete is the largest of the islands belonging to Greece, in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Deep red lips included in deception

indicators.note: included in places the edges inside the trickery word

parts.note: a con is a deception
lips are rims, as of cups

explanation.surface: Dark red lipstick used as part of a trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimson is a rich, deep shade of red, like that of blood.

clue.text: Browbeaten ambassador given a quick kiss by knight

parts.note: an ambassador is addressed as His Excellency, abbreviated HE
N is the chess notation for a knight
a peck is a quick kiss, so given one is pecked

explanation.surface: An intimidated diplomat receives a peck on the cheek from a knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Henpecked describes someone nagged and dominated, usually by a spouse, so cowed and bullied.

clue.text: After reform, Luddite weakened

indicators.note: after reform means once remodelled, so the letters take a new shape

explanation.surface: A technology hater lost strength after changing their ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Diluted means thinned or watered down, made weaker in strength or force.

clue.text: First in a line after soothsayer

indicators.note: after puts a and line behind the soothsayer

parts.note: taken as written
an augur foretold the future in ancient Rome

explanation.surface: Someone stands first in a queue behind a fortune-teller.
explanation.definitionFit: An inaugural event is the first of its kind, such as a maiden speech or opening ceremony.

clue.text: Information about artistic type

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A note gives details on a creative person.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre is a category or style of art, music or literature, a kind of type.

clue.text: Reason to record one Conservative

parts.note: to log something is to record it
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A justification for noting down a single Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: Logic is reasoning, the sound thinking process by which conclusions are reached.

clue.text: A Parisian left it in reverse before

parts.note: un is French for a, as a Parisian would say it

indicators.note: in reverse says the pair left and it are read backwards

explanation.surface: A Parisian left something in reverse gear before driving off.
explanation.definitionFit: Until means up to the time that, and in phrasing such as not until it works like before.

clue.text: Shy type, unexpectedly thriving, like son

indicators.note: unexpectedly signals the letters turn up in a surprising new order

explanation.surface: A timid person is surprisingly flourishing, just like their son.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrinking violet is an idiom for an excessively bashful or retiring person.

clue.text: Out of the running at present, at this point

parts.note: at present means now
at this point means here

explanation.surface: A race report: currently, at this stage, a contender has dropped out.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor finishing nowhere has failed to be placed at all, an idiom for losing badly.

clue.text: Stopped bandaging end of finger, puckered

indicators.note: bandaging means wrapping round, so the stopped word encloses the letter

parts.note: to stop is to cease

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of finger

explanation.surface: Someone stopped wrapping a fingertip, and the skin wrinkled.
explanation.definitionFit: Creased means folded or wrinkled, the same as puckered fabric or skin.
